title: Datagram loss lab: which knob dropped my datagrams?
blurb: Stress-tests configurable datagram bursts against WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream knobs (incomingHighWaterMark, incomingMaxAge, outgoingMaxAge) and diffs stats.datagrams before and after to attribute queue, expiry, and network loss.
question: Which stats.datagrams counters increment when a datagram burst overflows incomingHighWaterMark or ages past incomingMaxAge and outgoingMaxAge?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 behind --enable-blink-features=WebTransportStats against a local Deno QUIC echo server, bursts without reading incremented droppedIncoming by +149 to +196 while reading produced 0 loss; expiredIncoming was absent from all results even with incomingMaxAge set, and expiredOutgoing/lostOutgoing stayed 0 on loopback. Not verified unflagged in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 behind --enable-blink-features=WebTransportStats (local Deno QUIC echo server); not verified unflagged in Chrome 160

friction.summary: stats.datagrams.expiredIncoming was absent on Chrome 153 even when incomingMaxAge was configured
friction.repro: Set transport.datagrams.incomingMaxAge to a small positive value, send an unread datagram burst to an echo server, and inspect await transport.getStats(); datagrams contains droppedIncoming, expiredOutgoing, and lostOutgoing, but no expiredIncoming key.
friction.workaround: Check 'expiredIncoming' in stats.datagrams before reading it and treat an absent key as unreported rather than zero.
